questions.question: How does Databricks describe Agent Bricks in its late-2026 documentation?
choices: As a marketplace of prebuilt third-party agents that Databricks resells on a per-agent subscription
As its agent developer platform: runtime, memory, sandboxes, tools, tracing and gateway governance
As a no-code chatbot builder for business users, priced per seat and hosted inside Microsoft Teams
As the new name for Databricks SQL warehouses after they gained natural-language query support
questions.explanation: The Agent Bricks overview calls it 'the Databricks agent developer platform'. Its pieces include Agent Runtime, AgentKit for durable execution, Databricks Sandbox, Lakebase-backed memory and sessions, MCP servers and tools (including the Genie One MCP server), AI Search, MLflow Tracing, Unity Gateway and the Agent Bricks CLI. Business users get Genie; developers get Agent Bricks.

questions.question: Which Databricks product is aimed at business users who want to ask questions across company data without picking a specific curated agent?
choices: Databricks Apps, the serverless hosting service for Python and Node.js apps
Agent Bricks CLI, the command-line tool for deploying code-based agents
Genie Code, the developer assistant that writes notebooks and pipelines
Genie One
questions.explanation: Genie One is the business-user entry point. Genie Agents are curated domain agents that data teams build and tune; Genie Code is for developers; Agent Bricks is the developer platform for custom agents. In coaching, map each audience to its product before comparing with Copilot.

questions.question: A customer's 2025 architecture diagram says 'Mosaic AI Vector Search'. What do current Azure Databricks docs call it?
choices: Databricks AI Search, though REST paths and the vector_search() SQL function keep the old name
Genie Retrieval, since vector search is now available only inside Genie Agents
Unity Search, a feature of Unity Catalog that replaced standalone vector indexes entirely
Lakebase Vectors, after the vector engine moved into the managed Postgres service
questions.explanation: The docs now say 'Databricks AI Search (formerly Vector Search)'. The REST API (/api/2.0/vector-search/...), SDK services and the vector_search() SQL function still use the old name, so expect both names in customer code and slides.

questions.question: What do the current Azure Databricks docs call the AI governance layer that used to be called Mosaic AI Gateway?
choices: Model Firewall, a separate add-on product sold per endpoint
Lakehouse Monitoring for AI, part of Lakeflow Jobs
Agent Gateway, part of Databricks Apps
Unity Gateway, built on Unity Catalog
questions.explanation: The Learn page is titled 'AI governance with Unity Gateway'. Databricks' June 2026 blog URL and the Genie blog say 'Unity AI Gateway', and older model-serving pages still say 'AI Gateway'. They refer to the same governance layer, so expect all three names in customer conversations.

questions.question: Learn now labels Knowledge Assistant, Supervisor Agent and Information Extraction as 'legacy'. Where do those pages point new projects?
choices: Lakeflow Designer, which now builds agents as well as declarative data pipelines
Genie Agents for low-code document agents, and the Agent Bricks CLI for code-based agents
Mosaic AI Playground notebooks, exported to Model Serving as MLflow pyfunc models
Microsoft Copilot Studio, which Databricks now recommends for every agent built on Azure
questions.explanation: The legacy notice on these pages points to Genie Agents for new low-code document agents and to the Agent Bricks CLI for code-based agents. Existing agents keep working, but a customer starting fresh should not build on the legacy types.

questions.question: Beyond tables and volumes, which AI assets does Databricks say Unity Catalog now governs?
choices: Models, MCP services, agents and skills
Prompts only, while models and agents are governed by Microsoft Purview
Only dashboards and notebooks; AI assets are governed in each workspace separately
Nothing new: AI assets still live in the legacy workspace model registry
questions.explanation: Databricks' June 2026 Unity Gateway blog says Unity Catalog now covers governed models, MCP services, agents and skills. That's the core of the 'one governance layer for data and AI' argument versus stacks where data and agents are governed in different products.

questions.question: How does Databricks position MLflow on Databricks relative to open-source MLflow?
choices: It's a Microsoft-hosted service that Databricks resells under its own name
It's a closed fork with a proprietary trace format that can't be read by open-source MLflow
It's the same open-source product, managed and integrated with the platform
It's only for classical machine learning; GenAI tracing uses a separate Databricks product
questions.explanation: Databricks says 'MLflow on Databricks is MLflow', the same open-source product, managed and integrated. That matters for lock-in conversations: tracing and evaluation code written against MLflow isn't tied to one vendor.

questions.question: Where does Databricks recommend storing agent traces?
choices: In each user's browser storage, so that traces never leave the client device
Nowhere: traces are kept for 24 hours in memory and then discarded
In a separate Azure Monitor workspace, since traces can't be stored in the lakehouse
In Unity Catalog, where they're governed and queryable with SQL
questions.explanation: Databricks recommends storing traces in Unity Catalog so they're governed like data and queryable with SQL. Its DAIS 2026 material frames this as 'agent traces in the lakehouse', which supports audit and cost analysis.

questions.question: What is Lakebase?
choices: A data marketplace for buying third-party datasets
A serverless Spark cluster that's reserved for streaming ingestion jobs
A Delta Lake table format optimized for vector embeddings and similarity search
A fully managed Postgres database integrated with Databricks and Unity Catalog
questions.explanation: Learn describes Lakebase as 'a fully managed Postgres database integrated into the Databricks platform' with automatic scaling, instant branching and native Unity Catalog integration. For agents, it's the operational store: app state, agent memory and low-latency serving of lakehouse data.

questions.question: What are Databricks Apps?
choices: Python or Node.js data and AI apps hosted on serverless compute inside the Databricks platform
Mobile apps that Databricks publishes for iOS and Android, one per workspace
Notebook dashboards that refresh on a schedule and email results to every subscriber in the workspace each morning
Power Apps components that call Databricks through the Power Platform connector
questions.explanation: Databricks Apps let teams build and deploy secure data and AI applications on the platform. They run on serverless compute, support Python (Streamlit, Dash, Gradio) and Node.js (React, Angular, Svelte, Express) and need a Premium tier workspace. Agent Runtime also runs on Apps compute.

questions.question: What does Databricks Sandbox provide for agents, per Databricks' DAIS 2026 announcement?
choices: A free tier that gives each developer unlimited tokens for prototyping agents
A test workspace with synthetic data that's deleted automatically after 30 days
Secure VMs for agent code, with downscoped data access to Unity Catalog
A copy of production tables with all PII removed, refreshed weekly by Lakeflow
questions.explanation: Databricks' Agent Bricks blog says Databricks Sandbox spins up secure VMs with downscoped access to Unity Catalog. It lets agents run code without giving them broad data or network access.

questions.question: What backs the agent memory service Databricks announced for Agent Bricks?
choices: Azure Cosmos DB, provisioned in the customer's own subscription for each agent
Delta tables in a hidden system catalog that customers can't query
Lakebase
AI Search, which stores each conversation as an embedding in a vector index
questions.explanation: Databricks' blog describes an agent memory service powered by Lakebase, and Learn says Lakebase stores durable short- and long-term memory for agents built with LangGraph or the OpenAI Agents SDK. Memory stays in a Unity Catalog-registered database the customer controls.

questions.question: A team has agents written in LangGraph and the OpenAI Agents SDK. What does Databricks say about running them on Agent Bricks?
choices: Only LangChain agents are supported, so the OpenAI Agents SDK code has to be ported
They're supported, alongside Agno, CrewAI and the Claude Code SDK
They must be rewritten in a proprietary Databricks agent language before deployment
They can run only after export to ONNX and registration as classical ML models
questions.explanation: Databricks' DAIS 2026 blog lists LangGraph, Agno, CrewAI, the Claude Code SDK and OpenAI's agent SDKs. Agent code is wrapped in MLflow's ResponsesAgent interface, so the platform is framework-neutral. That helps when a customer worries about lock-in.

questions.question: How can a team switch the model behind a Databricks agent without changing the agent's code?
choices: It can't be done; models are compiled into the agent when it's first deployed
Open a support ticket so that Databricks swaps the model on the serving endpoint
Route its model calls through Unity Gateway and change the model there
Redeploy the agent with a new Databricks Runtime version, which picks a newer model
questions.explanation: The Agent Bricks docs say you can switch models without changing agent code through Unity Gateway. Databricks lists OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Qwen, Kimi and (through a SpaceX partnership) Grok models. That flexibility is a cost lever: route simple tasks to cheaper models.

questions.question: Which Genie items did Databricks say would enter private preview shortly after the June 2026 Data + AI Summit?
choices: Genie App Builder and Genie ZeroOps
Genie in Microsoft Teams and Genie in Slack, both limited to US regions
Genie One and Genie Agents, with general availability promised for 2027
Genie Code and Genie Ontology
questions.explanation: Databricks' Genie blog says Genie One, Genie Agents and Genie Code are generally available, and Genie App Builder and Genie ZeroOps are entering private preview. Don't promise preview features in a customer's production plan.

questions.question: What did Databricks announce as generally available under the name Document Intelligence at DAIS 2026?
choices: The ai_parse_document, ai_extract and ai_classify SQL functions
A Microsoft Word add-in that summarizes documents stored in SharePoint
An OCR appliance for on-premises scanners, priced per page
A document management system that replaces SharePoint for regulated content
questions.explanation: Databricks' Agent Bricks blog lists Document Intelligence (GA) as ai_parse_document, ai_extract and ai_classify. These run in SQL and pipelines, so document extraction can be a batch data job rather than a chat agent.

questions.question: Where can business users reach Genie One, per Databricks' June 2026 launch?
choices: Only in Microsoft Teams, because Databricks partnered exclusively with Microsoft for Genie
Only inside the Databricks workspace UI, because Genie One can't be embedded in other apps or reached from mobile devices
On the web, in native iOS and Android apps, in Slack and Microsoft Teams, and through a Genie MCP App
Only through Power BI, where Genie replaces the Q&A visual
questions.explanation: Databricks' Genie blog lists native iOS and Android apps, Slack and Microsoft Teams, and a Genie MCP App. That reach matters when a customer argues that Copilot wins simply because it's already in Teams.

questions.question: When you deploy a new code-based agent with the Agent Bricks CLI, where does it run?
choices: On Azure Container Apps in the customer's own subscription
On a pro SQL warehouse, since agents are compiled to SQL
On a classic all-purpose cluster that the developer must keep running
On Agent Runtime, which runs on Databricks Apps compute
questions.explanation: Learn says the Agent Bricks CLI serves the agent with DurableAgentServer and deploys it to Agent Runtime on Databricks Apps compute. Model Serving with agents.deploy() and the legacy MLflow AgentServer are documented as older paths.

questions.question: What is Omnigent?
choices: A Microsoft agent runtime that Databricks licenses for Azure Databricks only, and that's unavailable on AWS or Google Cloud
A Genie feature that merges every Genie Agent in a workspace into one
An evaluation benchmark that ranks agent frameworks by accuracy and by cost
Databricks' open-source agent meta-harness, with a managed version on Databricks in Beta
questions.explanation: Databricks' DAIS 2026 blog introduced Omnigent as a managed meta-harness, and the Unity Gateway blog lists Managed Omnigent on Databricks as Beta. Third-party recaps describe the harness itself as open source. Treat it as preview technology in customer plans.

questions.question: Which model providers does Databricks' DAIS 2026 Agent Bricks blog list as available?
choices: Only Azure OpenAI models, through the customer's own Azure subscription
Only Databricks' own DBRX models
Only open-weight Llama models, because proprietary models can't run on Databricks
OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Qwen and Kimi, plus Grok through a SpaceX partnership
questions.explanation: The blog lists OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and Qwen, adds Kimi, and adds Grok through a SpaceX partnership. Multi-model choice under one governance layer is a key contrast with suites tied to one model vendor.

questions.question: A customer asks which Databricks layer stops an agent from overspending on a frontier model and blocks prompts that contain PII. Which one is it?
choices: Databricks Apps, which caps app compute when an app's monthly budget runs out
Lakebase, because each agent's memory store also tracks its token spend
Unity Gateway
MLflow Tracing, which blocks calls after it scores them as unsafe
questions.explanation: Unity Gateway holds budgets (with hard caps that block usage), rate limits, usage tracking and service policies for guardrails such as PII and prompt-injection detection. MLflow observes and evaluates, Lakebase stores state and Apps host the agent; none of them enforces spend or content policy.

questions.question: What is Unity Catalog?
choices: Databricks' data marketplace, where customers buy and sell third-party datasets and prebuilt models
A file format for storing tables, similar to Parquet, that adds ACID transactions, schema checks and time travel
The Databricks workspace's home page, which lists every notebook, job and dashboard a user owns
Databricks' governance layer for data and AI: access control, row and column security, lineage and audit
questions.explanation: Unity Catalog governs tables, volumes, models, functions and agents' tools with a three-level namespace (catalog.schema.object), GRANT-based access control, row filters, column masks and ABAC policies, plus lineage and audit. Its policies apply wherever data is queried through Databricks, which is what makes Genie and agents governable.

questions.question: What is a DBU (Databricks Unit)?
choices: The normalized unit of compute Databricks bills by, with a rate that depends on workload type and tier
A credit that Databricks grants each user every month for free use of Genie and AI Functions
One gigabyte of data kept in Unity Catalog managed tables for one month in the customer's own cloud account
A fixed monthly fee per Databricks user, similar to a seat license for each workspace member
questions.explanation: Databricks bills compute in DBUs. The price per DBU depends on the workload (jobs, SQL, serverless, model serving) and the tier, and the cloud and region. To estimate cost, multiply the DBUs used by the customer's $/DBU rate.

questions.question: What are AI/BI dashboards in Databricks?
choices: Notebooks with charts that refresh automatically whenever their tables change
Power BI reports that Databricks generates automatically and publishes into a Fabric workspace
Databricks' built-in dashboards, governed by Unity Catalog and running on SQL warehouses
Monitoring pages that show the health and cost of model serving endpoints
questions.explanation: AI/BI dashboards are Databricks' native dashboards. They run on SQL warehouses, respect Unity Catalog permissions, and are often paired with Genie: the dashboard answers the standard questions, and Genie handles the follow-ups.

questions.question: What is Delta Sharing?
choices: A Unity Catalog setting that lets two workspaces in the same account see and edit each other's notebooks
A feature that emails a CSV extract of a table to a list of recipients on a schedule
A Genie option that lets one user share a conversation and its answers with a colleague
An open protocol for sharing live Delta data with other platforms and organizations without copying it
questions.explanation: Delta Sharing shares live Delta tables across platforms and organizations without making copies, and recipients don't need Databricks. Fabric doesn't mirror Delta Sharing tables, which matters in mixed estates.

questions.question: What is Lakehouse Federation?
choices: Unity Catalog's ability to query external systems as foreign catalogs without moving the data
A way to merge two Databricks accounts into one after a company acquisition
A replication service that copies external databases into Delta tables every night on a fixed schedule
A program that lets partners resell Databricks workspaces under their own brand
questions.explanation: Lakehouse Federation exposes external databases, and OneLake through catalog federation, as foreign catalogs in Unity Catalog. Databricks queries the data in place, and Unity Catalog grants control who can query it.

questions.question: What is Genie Code?
choices: A certification that data teams earn before they can publish Genie Agents
The SQL that Genie writes for each answer, which users can copy and paste into a notebook
The developer member of the Genie family: an AI assistant for building with code
The API key a developer needs before calling the Genie Conversation API
questions.explanation: Genie is a family: Genie One for business users, Genie Agents for curated domain analytics, and Genie Code for developers. Genie Code moved to pay-as-you-go billing with a free monthly allowance in July 2026, and the Genie One and Genie Agents promotion doesn't cover it.

questions.question: How many tables does Databricks recommend starting a Genie Agent with?
choices: Five or fewer, with a limited number of columns each
At least 50, because Genie gets more accurate as you add more tables
Every table in the catalog, since Genie selects relevant tables on its own
Exactly one wide denormalized table per agent, because joins aren't supported
questions.explanation: The curation guide says to aim for five or fewer tables and limit columns. The hard limit is 50 tables, views or metric views per agent. Above a handful of tables, prejoin into views or metric views. A focused agent beats a 'whole warehouse' agent.

questions.question: In what order does Databricks recommend adding context to a Genie Agent?
choices: Text instructions first, since natural language is what Genie understands best
SQL expressions for business semantics first, then example SQL, then text instructions as a last resort
Example SQL first, then table descriptions, then SQL expressions only if accuracy is still low
Benchmarks first, because Genie learns directly from the benchmark questions and their SQL
questions.explanation: The guide puts SQL expressions (measures, filters, fields) first, example SQL for complex or ambiguous questions second, and text instructions 'only as a last resort'. Structured context is more reliable than prose.

questions.question: What does Databricks say about Unity Catalog table and column descriptions for Genie?
choices: They're critical for accuracy, and AI-generated descriptions should be reviewed before use
They must be written in the Genie UI, since Unity Catalog comments aren't visible to Genie
They're ignored, because Genie reads only column names and data types
They're optional, because Genie samples every row to infer the meaning of each column
questions.explanation: Databricks calls table and column descriptions in Unity Catalog 'critical for Genie accuracy' and says to inspect AI-generated descriptions. Good metadata helps every Unity Catalog consumer, not just Genie, which is a useful point when a customer weighs the curation effort.

questions.question: A Genie Agent's text instructions say 'round currency to two decimals', but one example SQL query doesn't round. What's the risk?
choices: Conflicting guidance, which makes Genie's behavior inconsistent; examples should match instructions
The agent stops working until the conflict is fixed, because Genie validates instructions at save
Genie silently deletes the example query that conflicts with the instructions
None, because text instructions always override example SQL
questions.explanation: The curation guide warns against conflicting instructions and uses exactly this rounding example. If instructions say two decimals, example SQL should round to two decimals too. Conflicts are a common reason pilots look unreliable.

questions.question: What counts as a trusted asset in a Genie Agent?
choices: Dashboards that are published to Databricks One, which Genie copies into its answers
Answers that users have upvoted three or more times in the Monitor tab
Parameterized example SQL queries and Unity Catalog SQL functions that give verified answers
Any table with a Unity Catalog 'certified' tag, regardless of how the question is asked
questions.explanation: Trusted assets are example SQL queries and SQL functions that provide verified answers to anticipated questions. In Chat mode, when a parameterized example query produces the response, Genie marks it as a verified answer and users can change the parameter values and rerun.

questions.question: A Genie Agent uses a Unity Catalog SQL function as a trusted asset. What do the agent's users need, and what can Genie see?
choices: Users need MODIFY on the schema, and Genie rewrites the function when results look wrong
Users need EXECUTE on the function; Genie can call it but can't view or change its SQL
Users need CAN MANAGE on the agent, and Genie copies the function's SQL into its own answers
Users need nothing extra; Genie runs the function as the author and shows its SQL
questions.explanation: Agent users need EXECUTE on any SQL functions used. Genie can call registered functions but can't view or change their SQL, which makes functions a good way to lock down complex business logic. Scalar and table-valued functions are both supported.

questions.question: How many benchmark questions can a Genie Agent hold, and how should they be phrased?
choices: Unlimited, but each must have a unique SQL answer that isn't reused anywhere else
Up to 500, with two to four phrasings of each question sharing the same SQL answer
Up to 10, each phrased exactly as users will type it
Up to 50, written only by workspace admins and never by agent editors
questions.explanation: Genie allows up to 500 benchmark questions per agent. Databricks recommends two to four phrasings of each question using the same example SQL, so the benchmark tests understanding rather than exact wording.

questions.question: In a Chat mode benchmark run, which result does Genie grade as 'Bad'?
choices: Numeric values that match the SQL answer to four significant digits
The same rows as the SQL answer but in a different sort order
A result with extra columns compared with the SQL answer
Different SQL that returns exactly the same result set as the SQL answer
questions.explanation: Chat mode compares Genie's result with the SQL answer. Exact SQL matches, exact result-set matches, the same data in another order and numbers matching to four significant digits count as good. Empty results, errors, extra columns or a different single value count as bad. It compares up to 5,000 rows.

questions.question: How are Agent mode benchmark runs graded?
choices: By an LLM judge, guided by each question's evaluation note
They aren't graded; Agent mode can't be benchmarked
By comparing the generated SQL text character for character with the SQL answer
By the number of thumbs-up votes the answer received from users during the past week
questions.explanation: Chat mode compares results with SQL answers. Agent mode uses an LLM judge guided by the optional evaluation note. You pick the mode for each run, not for each question.

questions.question: Does Genie learn from its benchmark questions and SQL answers?
choices: Yes. Each benchmark run retrains Genie's model on the agent's SQL answers, so accuracy improves automatically over time
No. Benchmarks are only for evaluation; add example SQL or instructions to change behavior
Only in Agent mode, where failed questions automatically become instructions
Yes, but only for benchmark questions that were added from user chats
questions.explanation: Databricks' concepts page says Genie doesn't learn from benchmark questions or SQL. To improve answers, add example SQL, SQL expressions or trusted assets, then rerun the benchmarks to measure the change.

questions.question: A benchmark run finishes, but the Accuracy number is missing. Why?
choices: The run used Chat mode, which reports pass or fail and never a percentage
Benchmark results are visible only after a 24-hour processing delay
Accuracy appears only for workspace admins; agent editors see pass or fail counts but never the overall percentage
Some questions have no SQL answer and need manual review before accuracy is calculated
questions.explanation: Questions without a SQL answer need manual review, and the Accuracy number appears only after that review. Run details stay visible for a week. Budget reviewer time into a Genie rollout plan.

questions.question: What do business users need to use a published Genie Agent?
choices: Only a Microsoft Entra ID account; Genie grants data access automatically
CAN USE on a SQL warehouse plus a Databricks SQL Pro license for each user who asks questions
Consumer access or Databricks SQL, SELECT on the agent's data and CAN VIEW or CAN RUN on the agent
Workspace admin rights, since Genie generates SQL that only admins are allowed to run
questions.explanation: Consumers need consumer access or the Databricks SQL entitlement, SELECT on every Unity Catalog object the agent uses and at least CAN VIEW or CAN RUN on the agent. They don't need warehouse permissions, because the author's compute credentials are embedded.

questions.question: Whose identity does Genie use when it answers a question?
choices: A shared service principal for everything, with results filtered by Genie afterwards
The author's embedded credential for warehouse compute only, and the end user's identity for data access
The end user's identity for compute, so each user needs CAN USE on the warehouse
The author's identity for both compute and data, so every user sees exactly what the author can see in Unity Catalog tables
questions.explanation: Genie separates compute from data. The author's compute credential grants access to the warehouse only, while Unity Catalog evaluates data access as the end user. Queries are attributed to the end user in query history, and row filters and column masks apply per user.

questions.question: A user without SELECT on a table asks a Genie Agent a question that needs that table. What happens?
choices: Genie returns the data anyway, because the author's credential is used for data access
Genie emails the table owner a request to grant access automatically
The agent is disabled for all users until the grant is fixed
They get an empty response rather than a permissions error
questions.explanation: Without access the response is empty. That's secure, but it can look like a wrong answer, so pilot teams should check grants first when users report empty results.

questions.question: What happens to entity matching on a table that has row filters or column masks?
choices: It runs as the author, so all users benefit from the author's broader access
It's disabled, so Genie doesn't sample values that some users can't see
Nothing changes; entity matching ignores Unity Catalog policies
It's enabled, but only for workspace admins
questions.explanation: Databricks disables entity matching on tables with row filters or column masks. It's a deliberate trade-off: slightly weaker value matching in exchange for not leaking restricted values through prompts.

questions.question: An author hides a sensitive column in a Genie Agent. Who can still see the column's data?
choices: No one, because hiding a column in the Genie Agent also revokes SELECT on that column in Unity Catalog for every user
Only workspace admins, and only through the Genie UI
Only the agent's author, through the Genie Monitor tab
Anyone with SELECT who queries the table directly; hiding doesn't change Unity Catalog permissions
questions.explanation: Hiding a column only shapes what the agent uses. It doesn't change Unity Catalog permissions, so use column masks or grants to protect sensitive data.

questions.question: What's the key difference between Genie Chat mode and Agent mode?
choices: Chat mode answers only from dashboards; Agent mode answers only from raw tables
Chat mode runs read-only SQL on structured data; Agent mode adds documents in volumes and MCP connectors
Chat mode is for business users and writes results back to tables; Agent mode is read-only and limited to admins and editors
Chat mode uses Copilot's model; Agent mode uses a Databricks model
questions.explanation: Chat mode handles structured data with read-only SQL and can't read PDFs or Word files. Agent mode adds volumes and MCP connectors, streams its reasoning and produces reports with citations.

questions.question: Which items count toward a Genie Agent's 100-instruction limit?
choices: Each benchmark question and each user conversation
Each table, each column description and each synonym, since all agent metadata counts against the same limit
Each synonym and each entity-matching column
Each example SQL query, each SQL function and the general instructions block
questions.explanation: The 100-instruction limit counts each example SQL query, each SQL function and the general instructions block. A separate limit allows 200 knowledge store snippets (table descriptions, joins, SQL expressions); column descriptions and synonyms don't count toward it.

questions.question: How many general text instruction blocks can a Genie Agent have?
choices: Unlimited, but only five are read per question
One
Up to 100
One per table in the agent
questions.explanation: An agent has at most one general text instruction block, which the API validates. Put business logic in SQL expressions and example SQL instead of long prose.

questions.question: Which groups of APIs does the Genie Conversation API documentation describe?
choices: Only management APIs; asking questions from code isn't supported
Read-only APIs for exporting past conversations to Microsoft Purview
Chat mode APIs, Agent mode APIs and management APIs for creating and deploying agents
A single REST endpoint that returns a CSV answer for each question, with no conversation state or management functions
questions.explanation: Chat mode APIs support stateful conversations and return SQL, results and visualizations. Agent mode APIs stream reasoning and return reports with citations. Management APIs create and configure agents for CI/CD.

questions.question: A developer calls the Genie Management API. Which old term still appears in the endpoint path?
choices: spaces, as in /api/2.0/genie/spaces
lakeview, as in /api/2.0/lakeview/genie
rooms, as in /api/2.0/genie/rooms
assistants, as in /api/2.0/assistants/genie
questions.explanation: Genie Agents were formerly Genie spaces, and the management endpoints still say 'spaces' (POST /api/2.0/genie/spaces). Expect old names in automation scripts.

questions.question: What does the Genie Conversation API documentation say about retries and polling?
choices: The API retries failed questions automatically up to 10 times
Clients must poll exactly once per minute, or the conversation is closed
The API doesn't retry for you; poll every 1 to 5 seconds with backoff and add your own retries
Polling isn't needed, because every answer returns synchronously within one second
questions.explanation: The docs say to add your own retry with exponential backoff. They recommend polling every 1 to 5 seconds, backing off to one minute, with a 10-minute cap. Build this into any custom app or Copilot integration that calls Genie directly.

questions.question: Which authentication does Databricks recommend for a user-facing app that calls the Genie Conversation API?
choices: OAuth user-to-machine, so each question runs with the signed-in user's identity
A personal access token for the app owner, shared by all users so the app doesn't need a sign-in flow
OAuth machine-to-machine with one service principal for every user
Anonymous access with an API key in the URL
questions.explanation: The docs recommend OAuth U2M for user-facing apps and M2M with a service principal only when no browser is available. U2M keeps per-user Unity Catalog enforcement. Service principal usage is billed and isn't covered by Genie's free promotion.

questions.question: How is a metric view different from a standard view?
choices: It's a temporary view that's deleted when the session ends
It stores precomputed results that refresh every minute, so queries never touch the underlying source tables
It can only be read by Power BI, not by Genie or SQL
It defines measures and dimensions once, so users can group by any field at query time
questions.explanation: Standard views fix aggregations and groupings when they're created. Metric views define measures and dimensions once and let users group by any field. Genie can use them as table-like sources, and Databricks calls them particularly effective for Genie Agents.

questions.question: How do you query a measure from a metric view in SQL?
choices: Measures can't be queried in SQL; they're for Genie only
Wrap it in the MEASURE() function
Select it as a normal column, which returns pre-aggregated totals
Call the metric view as a table-valued function with the measure name
questions.explanation: Measures use aggregate functions and are queried with MEASURE(). The YAML defines version, source, joins, fields (also called dimensions), measures, filters and optional materialization, so the logic is defined once and reused by BI, SQL and Genie.

questions.question: Can a metric view's YAML filter use current_user() to show each person only their own rows?
choices: No, because metric views can't be secured at all
Yes, and it's the recommended way to secure Genie Agents, since filters in metric views override Unity Catalog row filters
No; invoker functions aren't allowed there, so use Unity Catalog row filters for per-user security
Yes, but only for materialized metric views
questions.explanation: The YAML reference says the filter can't use invoker-dependent functions such as current_user(). Per-user security belongs in Unity Catalog row filters and column masks, which Genie enforces per user.

questions.question: A pilot user notices Genie wrote slightly different SQL for the same question on two days. What does Databricks say about this?
choices: It means the warehouse was restarted, which resets Genie's memory
Genie is non-deterministic; example SQL reduces variation but doesn't eliminate it
It's a bug, since Genie caches every question and must return identical SQL
It happens only when benchmarks haven't been run in the past week
questions.explanation: Genie is non-deterministic. Example SQL and trusted assets reduce variation, and parameterized trusted queries give verified answers. Set that expectation early with stakeholders.

questions.question: What does someone need to create or edit a Genie Agent?
choices: Account admin rights and a classic all-purpose cluster
Only SELECT on the data, since warehouses are chosen automatically
Only a Genie One license, which includes authoring rights, plus account admin approval for each new agent the author creates
Databricks SQL, CAN USE on a pro or serverless warehouse, SELECT on the data and CAN EDIT on the agent
questions.explanation: Authors need the Databricks SQL entitlement, CAN USE on at least one pro or serverless SQL warehouse, SELECT on the data and at least CAN EDIT on the agent. Creators get CAN MANAGE.

questions.question: How does Databricks recommend deploying and versioning Genie Agents across environments?
choices: By copying and pasting each agent's settings into the target workspace by hand
As code, with bundles and the management API for CI/CD
By exporting a PDF of the agent and importing it into the target workspace
Agents can't be moved; each environment must be configured by hand from scratch
questions.explanation: The curation guide recommends deploying and versioning agents as code with bundles, and the management APIs support CI/CD. That gives Genie the same promotion path as other governed assets.

questions.question: What role does a Databricks SQL warehouse play when someone asks Genie a question?
choices: It stores a copy of the data that Genie is allowed to answer from
It keeps the conversation history so Genie can learn from it
It's the compute that runs the SQL Genie writes, billed in DBUs
It hosts the language model that turns the question into SQL
questions.explanation: Genie turns a question into SQL, and a SQL warehouse runs that SQL against Unity Catalog tables. The warehouse is billed in DBUs, separately from Genie's own AI usage, so a Genie rollout needs a warehouse budget even while AI usage is free.

questions.question: What's the difference between Genie One and a Genie Agent?
choices: Genie One answers from documents only; a Genie Agent answers from tables only and never from documents
Genie One is for developers writing code; a Genie Agent is for business users asking questions
They're the same thing: 'Genie One' is the new name that Genie Agents took in late 2026
Genie One is a broad coworker for business users; a Genie Agent is a curated Genie for one domain
questions.explanation: Genie One is the agentic coworker for business users across governed data and connected apps. A Genie Agent (formerly a Genie space) is built by a data team from chosen tables, metric views, instructions and example SQL for a specific domain. Copilot Studio connects to Genie Agents one at a time by ID.

questions.question: Genie keeps getting 'fiscal quarter' wrong because the company's fiscal year starts in July. What's the best first fix?
choices: Define fiscal quarter once in the Genie Agent, for example as a SQL expression or in a metric view
Ask users to add 'our fiscal year starts in July' to the end of every question they ask
Load a benchmark of fiscal questions, which Genie learns from overnight to fix its answers
Retrain Genie's underlying model on the company's past finance reports so it learns the fiscal calendar
questions.explanation: Databricks recommends adding business semantics as SQL expressions first, then example SQL, then text instructions. A metric view or SQL expression that defines fiscal quarter makes every answer consistent. Genie doesn't retrain on your data, and benchmarks only measure accuracy.

questions.question: A Genie Agent answers for most users, but some get a permission error on one table. What's the likely cause?
choices: Genie runs as the agent's creator, whose session has expired
The table is too big for Genie, so it errors for users with fewer rows
Those users lack SELECT on the table, or USE CATALOG and USE SCHEMA on its parents
Genie caps each agent at 50 users, and the extra users are refused
questions.explanation: Genie runs queries as the asking user, so Unity Catalog permissions apply. Querying a table needs SELECT on it plus USE CATALOG and USE SCHEMA on its catalog and schema. Grant through groups so new users don't hit the same wall.

questions.question: A data lead says, 'Once we load benchmarks, Genie will learn from them and get better.' What's accurate?
choices: Benchmarks improve Genie only for the user who wrote them, not for anyone else who uses the agent
Benchmarks only measure; better answers come from SQL expressions, example SQL and metric views
Genie learns from benchmarks only if the agent is in Agent mode, never in Chat mode
That's right: Genie retrains on its benchmark questions every night and improves within a week
questions.explanation: Genie doesn't learn from benchmarks. They're up to 500 test questions, ideally with SQL answers, that measure accuracy so you can see whether a change helped. To improve answers, add SQL expressions, example SQL, trusted assets, instructions or metric views, then rerun the benchmarks.

questions.question: Which of these claims about Genie would be wrong to make to a customer?
choices: Genie answers from a copy of your data, so permissions are checked once at setup
Genie enforces Unity Catalog permissions on every answer using the asker's identity
A Genie Agent can include up to 50 tables, views or metric views
Genie has no per-seat price; compute is billed separately
questions.explanation: Genie queries data in place and checks permissions on every answer with the asking user's identity, so row filters and column masks stay in force. The other three statements are accurate. A wrong claim about security is the fastest way to lose a security team's trust.

questions.question: Where in a Genie answer are Unity Catalog row filters actually enforced?
choices: When the Genie Agent is created, for the creator
When the data is copied into Genie each night
When Genie formats the answer, by hiding rows
When the generated SQL runs on the warehouse, for the asking user's identity
questions.explanation: Genie writes SQL, and the SQL runs on a warehouse against Unity Catalog tables as the asking user. Row filters and column masks are applied at query time, so two people asking the same question can get different results. Nothing is copied into Genie.

questions.question: Which knowledge sources can an Agent Bricks Knowledge Assistant use?
choices: Only web pages, which it crawls nightly from a list of public URLs supplied by the author
Only SharePoint sites, through a Microsoft Graph connector that's configured by an admin
Only Genie Agents, since Knowledge Assistant can't read documents directly
Files in a Unity Catalog volume, a Unity Catalog table with a content column, or an AI Search index
questions.explanation: Knowledge Assistant reads files in a UC volume (txt, pdf, md, ppt/pptx, doc/docx), a UC table with a binary or string content column, or an AI Search index, up to 10 sources. It answers with citations. Learn now labels it legacy and points new low-code document agents to Genie Agents.

questions.question: Which files does Knowledge Assistant skip?
choices: Any file older than one year
Files that contain tables or images
Any file that's not in English
Files over 100 MB, and PDF, DOC or PPT files over 500 pages
questions.explanation: Knowledge Assistant skips files over 100 MB and PDF, DOC or PPT files over 500 pages. ai_parse_document has the same 500-page and 100 MB limits. Check large manuals and contracts in a customer's corpus.

questions.question: How do subject-matter experts improve a Knowledge Assistant's answers?
choices: By retraining the underlying model on the documents, which takes several days per run
By adding natural-language guidelines to labeled questions, which take effect right after they're saved
By editing the vector embeddings directly in the AI Search index
They can't; quality depends only on the documents
questions.explanation: Experts add natural-language guidelines to labeled questions, and Databricks says these apply right after they're saved. Labeled data can be imported or exported as a UC table, and an evaluation notebook can use curated datasets and custom scorers.

questions.question: How many subagents and tools can a Supervisor Agent coordinate?
choices: Up to 10
Up to 50
Unlimited
Up to 3
questions.explanation: Supervisor Agent coordinates up to 50 subagents and tools: Genie Agents, published dashboards, Knowledge Assistant and other serving endpoints, UC functions, tables and volumes, AI Search indexes, other Supervisor Agents, UC MCP services, custom MCP servers and custom agents on Databricks Apps.

questions.question: What can Supervisor Agent's built-in code execution reach?
choices: Write access to any table the agent's author owns
No internet, and read-only access to UC tables and volumes added as tools, per the end user's rights
The public internet and every table in the metastore, using the agent author's permissions rather than the end user's
Only the author's local laptop, through a tunnel
questions.explanation: The built-in code execution has no internet access and read-only access to the UC tables and volumes added as tools, subject to the end user's permissions. Supervisor Agent also has no native web search.

questions.question: A user can access two of a Supervisor Agent's five subagents. What happens when they ask a question that needs the other three?
choices: They're kept away from the subagents they can't access; users with no access have the chat ended
The supervisor fails the whole request and disables the agent
The supervisor asks an admin to approve temporary access
The supervisor answers anyway, using the author's access to all five subagents, and logs the request for later review
questions.explanation: Supervisor Agent has built-in access controls, so end users only reach the subagents and data they can access. Users with access to none have the conversation ended. Permissions follow the user, not the author.

questions.question: Which limitation applies to AI Search indexes used as Supervisor Agent subagents?
choices: Only indexes with fewer than 1,000 documents are supported
Only Delta Sync indexes are supported
Only Direct Vector Access indexes are supported
AI Search indexes can't be used at all
questions.explanation: Supervisor Agent supports Delta Sync indexes only for AI Search subagents, and it has no native web search.

questions.question: Who can use a newly created Agent Bricks agent by default?
choices: Everyone in the workspace, since Agent Bricks agents are shared with all workspace users by default
Only its authors and workspace admins, until Can Query or Can Manage is granted
Only account admins, regardless of who built the agent
Everyone in the Entra tenant, through Microsoft Teams
questions.explanation: By default only authors and workspace admins have access. Can Manage lets a user configure the agent, set permissions and improve quality. Can Query allows Playground and API use but not viewing or editing on the Agents page.

questions.question: What do the Agent Bricks agent types require before you can build one?
choices: Serverless compute and access to a serverless usage policy with a nonzero budget
A Microsoft 365 Copilot license for the author
A dedicated Azure OpenAI deployment in the same region
A classic all-purpose cluster with at least eight GPUs, reserved for the author for the life of the agent
questions.explanation: The Agent Bricks pages require serverless compute and a serverless usage policy with a nonzero budget. Admins can use serverless usage policies to control who can build these agents and how their spend is attributed.

questions.question: When setting up Information Extraction, what model choice does the author make?
choices: No choice, because the extraction model is fixed
GPT-4 or Llama 2
Optimize for Scale (default) or Optimize for Complexity
Any model from Hugging Face, uploaded by the author
questions.explanation: Step 1 offers 'Optimize for Scale' (default) or 'Optimize for Complexity'. The feature has a 128k-token context, isn't supported with Enhanced Security and Compliance, and is in Beta. The newer GA path is the ai_extract SQL function.

questions.question: What does DurableAgentServer add over the legacy MLflow AgentServer?
choices: Automatic translation of agents into Copilot Studio topics
Persistent run state, crash recovery, idempotent invocations and ordered sessions
A graphical designer for drag-and-drop agent building, plus automatic export of agents to Copilot Studio
Free model tokens for the first 30 days after deployment
questions.explanation: DurableAgentServer, used by the Agent Bricks CLI and Agent Runtime, adds persistent run state, crash recovery, idempotent invocations and ordered sessions. Long-running agents need these to survive failures without duplicating side effects.

questions.question: What is MLflow's ResponsesAgent?
choices: A hosted chatbot that answers questions about MLflow's documentation and can be embedded in any Databricks App
MLflow's recommended interface for wrapping agent code, compatible with the OpenAI Responses schema
A scoring judge that rates agent responses from 1 to 5
A Copilot Studio connector that calls MLflow experiments
questions.explanation: Databricks recommends ResponsesAgent for authoring. It supports streaming, custom inputs and outputs, multi-agent setups and tool-call messages, and it's compatible with the OpenAI Responses schema. Any framework can sit inside it.

questions.question: A developer deploys an agent on Databricks Apps but it doesn't appear in the workspace Agents list. What's the likely cause?
choices: The agent wasn't registered in Microsoft Entra ID
The agent wasn't approved by a Genie Agent owner
The app name doesn't start with the prefix 'agent-'
The developer used Python rather than Node.js
questions.explanation: Agents must be named with the prefix 'agent-' to appear in the workspace Agents list. It's a small detail that causes confusion in pilots.

questions.question: What must you do before calling agents.deploy() to put an agent on Model Serving?
choices: Create a Genie Agent with the same name
Convert it to a SQL function
Publish it to the Microsoft Agent Store and wait for approval
Register the agent in Unity Catalog as a model version
questions.explanation: The deploy page says to register the agent in Unity Catalog first, then call agents.deploy(uc_model_name, version). Registering makes the agent a governed UC asset with versions and permissions.

questions.question: Besides the serving endpoint, what does agents.deploy() set up?
choices: A Microsoft Teams app, a Copilot Studio agent and a Power BI semantic model of the agent's answers, each created automatically
A Review App, real-time tracing, inference tables, scoped credentials and optional monitoring
A nightly job that retrains the agent's model on its own logs
A dedicated SQL warehouse reserved for the agent
questions.explanation: agents.deploy() creates the endpoint with autoscaling, short-lived credentials for Databricks resources, the Review App, real-time tracing to the active experiment, inference tables, REST and feedback logging, and optional production monitoring (beta). Deployments can take up to 15 minutes.

questions.question: How do you update a Model Serving agent with zero downtime?
choices: Delete the endpoint and create a new one with the same name and settings
Stop the endpoint, upload new code and restart it
Deploy a new version under the same UC model name and change nothing else
Zero-downtime updates aren't supported
questions.explanation: Deploying a new version of the same UC model adds it to the existing endpoint and shifts traffic once it's ready. Zero downtime requires changing nothing except the model version.

questions.question: What's the trade-off when you set scale_to_zero_enabled=True on an agent endpoint?
choices: No trade-off; it's recommended for every production agent
Higher cost but faster responses, because idle endpoints are billed at a premium rate
Lower cost, but tracing is disabled
Lower cost when idle, but slower responses to the first queries after idle time
questions.explanation: Scale to zero reduces cost but increases the time to serve initial queries. It suits dev and low-traffic agents. For latency-sensitive production agents, keep a minimum warm.

questions.question: What does MLflow Tracing capture for each agent request?
choices: Only the final answer and the user's name, because intermediate steps are discarded to protect privacy and reduce storage
Screenshots of the user's screen during the request
Only errors; successful requests aren't traced
Each step (model calls, tool calls, retrieval) with inputs, outputs, latency, tokens and cost
questions.explanation: MLflow Tracing records each step (model calls, tool calls, retrieval) with inputs, outputs, latency, token usage and cost. Traces are the raw material for debugging, evaluation, cost analysis and audit.

questions.question: An agent deployed from a notebook in a Databricks Git folder isn't producing real-time traces. Why?
choices: Tracing works only for agents written in Scala
Real-time tracing doesn't work by default there; set a non-Git experiment before deploying
Git folders encrypt every trace with the repository's key, so traces exist but can't be read by MLflow in the workspace
Tracing requires a Premium Copilot license
questions.explanation: The deploy page says real-time tracing doesn't work by default for notebooks in a Git folder. Call mlflow.set_experiment() with a non-Git experiment before agents.deploy().

questions.question: What are MLflow scorers?
choices: Leaderboards comparing public models
Billing meters that count tokens per agent
Human raters hired by Databricks to grade each agent on a five-point scale
LLM judges and code-based checks that attach feedback to each trace
questions.explanation: Scorers are LLM judges and code-based checks attached to traces as feedback. Prebuilt LLM judges include Correctness, Completeness and Fluency, and you can register custom scorers. The same scorers run with mlflow.genai.evaluate() on evaluation datasets and on production traffic.

questions.question: Business reviewers need to give feedback on an agent deployed on Databricks Apps. Which tool should they use?
choices: MLflow labeling sessions, since the Review App doesn't support Apps-deployed agents
The Review App, which works for every deployment type including Databricks Apps
Genie benchmarks
A Microsoft Forms survey linked from the agent
questions.explanation: The Review App doesn't support agents deployed on Databricks Apps, so use labeling sessions on existing traces. Feedback can also be logged with the log_feedback API.

questions.question: What's the status of MLflow production monitoring for agents, which runs scorers on live traffic?
choices: Deprecated
Beta
Generally available since 2023
Available only in AWS regions
questions.explanation: Production monitoring is labeled beta. It runs the same scorers used in development on live traffic, so quality drift shows up without manual spot checks.

questions.question: Which logging features does the deploy page mark as deprecated, and what replaces them?
choices: Unity Catalog lineage; it's replaced by Purview
Request logs, assessment logs and the feedback model, replaced by MLflow 3 tracing and log_feedback
MLflow tracing; it's replaced by request logs
Inference tables and Unity Catalog lineage, which are replaced by Azure Monitor and Microsoft Purview for all agent logging
questions.explanation: Request logs, assessment logs and the feedback model are deprecated. Use MLflow 3 real-time tracing and the log_feedback API. All agents use AI Gateway inference tables for payload logging.

questions.question: How do Databricks agents reach Unity Catalog functions and AI Search indexes as tools?
choices: Through ODBC connections that the agent opens at startup with the deploying developer's personal access token
They can't; tools must be written in Python inside the agent
Through Power Automate flows
Through workspace managed MCP endpoints such as /api/2.0/mcp/functions/<catalog>/<schema>
questions.explanation: Managed MCP endpoints expose UC functions (/api/2.0/mcp/functions/...) and AI Search indexes (/api/2.0/mcp/ai-search/...; the older vector-search path still works). Agents can also use custom and external MCP servers and the Genie One MCP server.

questions.question: Which agent tools need no resource grant in databricks.yml?
choices: Genie Agents, since they're Databricks resources with their own permissions
Local Python function tools that run inside the agent process
Unity Catalog functions
SQL warehouses
questions.explanation: Local function tools (@function_tool in the OpenAI Agents SDK, @tool in LangChain) run in-process and need no grant. Databricks resources such as Genie Agents, UC functions, warehouses and indexes must be declared so the app's service principal gets permissions.

questions.question: How does a streaming Databricks agent report an error that happens mid-stream?
choices: Errors are silently dropped
With an HTTP 500 status before the stream begins, so the client never receives partial output
By emailing the agent owner
In the last token, under databricks_output.error, which the client must handle
questions.explanation: Streaming errors arrive in the last token under databricks_output.error. Client apps, including custom Teams or Copilot front ends, need to check for it.

questions.question: Which model customization techniques does Databricks' DAIS 2026 Agent Bricks blog mention?
choices: Only RAG; fine-tuning was removed
Only full pretraining of new foundation models on the customer's own data
Only prompt templates; models can't be customized
Prompt optimization, fine-tuning and reinforcement learning
questions.explanation: The blog says customers can customize models with prompt optimization, fine-tuning or reinforcement learning. Pair any of these with evaluation datasets so you can measure the gain against the cost.

questions.question: A team has a LangGraph agent that runs long tasks and must survive crashes without repeating work. Where should it run on Databricks?
choices: On Agent Runtime, deployed with the Agent Bricks CLI, which serves it with DurableAgentServer
In an AI/BI dashboard, using a scheduled refresh to trigger each step of the agent's work in order
On a classic all-purpose cluster, started by hand whenever the agent needs to run a task
On a Genie Agent, pasting the LangGraph code into its instructions so that Genie runs it
questions.explanation: New code-based agents are built and deployed with the Agent Bricks CLI and run on Agent Runtime. DurableAgentServer adds persistent run state, crash recovery, idempotent invocations and ordered sessions. Older MLflow AgentServer and Model Serving deployment paths are labeled legacy.

questions.question: MLflow scorers and Genie benchmarks both measure quality. What does each measure?
choices: Scorers grade any agent's traces in development and production; benchmarks test a Genie Agent's answers
Scorers measure only latency and cost; benchmarks measure only whether the SQL ran without error
Scorers test a Genie Agent's answers to set questions; benchmarks grade any agent's traces in production
They're the same tool: benchmarks are simply what MLflow scorers are called inside the Genie UI
questions.explanation: MLflow scorers, including LLM judges and code-based checks, grade traces from any agent, on evaluation datasets and on live traffic. Genie benchmarks are up to 500 test questions for one Genie Agent, ideally with SQL answers, to measure its accuracy. Neither trains the model; they tell you whether changes helped.

questions.question: Which capabilities does the Unity Gateway overview list?
choices: Usage tracking, inference tables, rate limits, fallbacks, budgets, cost analysis and guardrail policies
Seat licensing, user provisioning and Microsoft 365 group sync for Genie users
Model training, fine-tuning and hyperparameter search for custom foundation models, plus GPU scheduling across workspaces
Only API key storage for external providers, with no logging, limits or policy features
questions.explanation: The overview lists usage tracking in system tables, request and response logging to Unity Catalog Delta tables (inference tables), rate limits, traffic splitting and fallbacks, budgets with per-user thresholds and hard caps, cost analysis by model, principal and tag, service policies for guardrails and Smart Routing for coding tasks.

questions.question: Which kinds of AI services does Unity Gateway govern?
choices: Hosted and external models, UC-registered models, MCP tools, UC functions and HTTP connections
Only Databricks-hosted open-weight models; external providers must be governed elsewhere
Only Microsoft Foundry deployments connected to Azure Databricks through Private Link, plus Copilot Studio agents
Only Genie Agents, because other agents are governed by Microsoft Agent 365
questions.explanation: The overview covers system.ai model services (Foundation Model APIs, no setup), external model providers (bring your own key), Unity Catalog registered models, MCP tools, custom tools as UC functions and HTTP connections. Agents are governed as UC registered models, and their tools as MCP services, functions and connections.

questions.question: Which risks do Unity Gateway's AI guardrails address, per Databricks' June 2026 blog?
choices: PII exposure, prompt injection, jailbreaks, unsafe content and other policy violations
Only profanity in model outputs, using a fixed English word list that admins can extend
Only cost overruns; content safety is left to each model provider
Only malware in uploaded files, scanned by Microsoft Defender
questions.explanation: The blog lists PII exposure, prompt injection, jailbreaks, unsafe content and other policy violations. Guardrails can be built-in, custom or from external partners through service policies.

questions.question: What can Unity Gateway's Contextual Service Policies (Beta) do?
choices: Only rate-limit requests per endpoint, with no awareness of who's calling or what's in the request
Rewrite prompts into shorter versions to save tokens before they reach the model
Allow, deny or require approval based on user, agent, model, MCP service, tool or request content
Assign Copilot Credits to agents according to their business priority
questions.explanation: Contextual Service Policies, labeled Beta in the June 2026 blog, allow, deny or require approval based on the user, agent, model, MCP service, tool or request and response content. The blog's example blocks PII from being published while allowing it to be emailed.

questions.question: Which Databricks-managed MCP services did the June 2026 Unity Gateway blog list?
choices: Salesforce, SAP and Workday only
None; MCP services must be custom-built and self-hosted
Google Drive, Jira, Confluence, Slack, GitHub and SharePoint
Only Databricks SQL and Genie, with no third-party systems
questions.explanation: The blog lists Databricks-managed MCP services for Google Drive, Jira, Confluence, Slack, GitHub and SharePoint, and says custom MCP services can be registered in Unity Catalog. That puts third-party tool access under the same governance as data.

questions.question: An agent calls an MCP service registered through Unity Gateway at /ai-gateway/mcp-services/<catalog>.<schema>.<service>. Which privileges does the caller need?
choices: SELECT on the service and MODIFY on the schema
CAN MANAGE on the workspace
EXECUTE on the service, plus USE CATALOG and USE SCHEMA
None, because MCP services are public within the account
questions.explanation: MCP services through Unity Gateway are Unity Catalog objects. The caller needs EXECUTE plus USE CATALOG and USE SCHEMA, the same privilege model as UC functions.

questions.question: What are inference tables in Unity Gateway?
choices: Temporary caches of embeddings that are deleted after each request completes
Billing tables that list the price of each model by region
Unity Catalog Delta tables that log the requests and responses passing through governed endpoints
Tables of model benchmark scores that Databricks publishes every month for each hosted foundation model
questions.explanation: Inference tables log request and response payloads to Unity Catalog Delta tables for audit and analysis. Model Serving limits note that requests or responses over 1 MB aren't logged.

questions.question: What's the difference between app authorization and user authorization for agents on Databricks Apps?
choices: There's no difference; the two names refer to the same setting in different UI pages
App authorization uses personal access tokens; user authorization uses Microsoft Entra passwords
App authorization is for admins and user authorization is for developers; both use the developer's token
App authorization uses the app's service principal for everyone; user authorization acts as each calling user
questions.explanation: App authorization (previously service principal authentication) is the default: Databricks creates a service principal and all users share its permissions. User authorization (previously on-behalf-of, OBO) acts as the calling user and enforces Unity Catalog row filters and column masks per user.

questions.question: What's the status of user authorization (formerly on-behalf-of-user) for Databricks Apps agents?
choices: Deprecated, with no replacement planned for agents on Databricks Apps
Private preview, available only on AWS
Public Preview, and a workspace admin must enable it
Generally available and on by default for every workspace and every app
questions.explanation: User authorization is in Public Preview and needs a workspace admin to enable it. Scopes such as sql, genie, model-serving and ai-gateway are added under user_api_scopes, and changes can take up to five minutes to propagate.

questions.question: A developer uses user authorization, but the forwarded user token is missing. What does get_user_workspace_client() do?
choices: It silently falls back to the app's service principal, so test with a whoami tool
It prompts the user to sign in again in a pop-up window
It raises an error and the request fails, so the problem is obvious in testing
It uses the workspace admin's identity
questions.explanation: If the forwarded token is missing, get_user_workspace_client() falls back to the service principal without raising. The docs suggest a whoami tool that must return your username, not a UUID, and removing it before production. A silent fallback can quietly turn per-user access into shared access.

questions.question: Where in an agent's code should get_user_workspace_client() be called?
choices: Inside the request handler, because no user context exists at startup
In the client browser
In a scheduled job that refreshes tokens every hour
Once at startup, then cached and reused for all users to save time on each request
questions.explanation: The downscoped user token arrives per request in the x-forwarded-access-token header. Call get_user_workspace_client() inside the @invoke or @stream handler. A client created at startup would have no user context.

questions.question: Can one agent use both app authorization and user authorization?
choices: Only for Genie Agents
Only if the agent runs on a classic cluster
No; an app must choose one authorization method for all of its resources when it's first created
Yes; for example, app authorization for a shared index and user authorization for user-specific tables
questions.explanation: Both methods can be combined. A common pattern is app authorization for shared, non-sensitive resources and user authorization wherever per-user Unity Catalog enforcement matters.

questions.question: Which minimum permission does an agent's identity need on a Genie Agent it calls?
choices: OWNER
MODIFY on the agent's catalog
CAN MANAGE
CAN RUN
questions.explanation: The permission table lists CAN RUN on a Genie Agent, CAN QUERY on a serving endpoint, EXECUTE on a UC function, CAN USE on a SQL warehouse and SELECT on tables and AI Search indexes. Granting access to a Genie Agent also requires its downstream tables, warehouse and functions.

questions.question: An agent's service principal has CAN RUN on a Genie Agent, but answers come back empty. What's likely missing?
choices: Nothing; empty answers mean the data really is empty
A Lakebase database to cache the Genie Agent's earlier answers
A Microsoft 365 Copilot license for the service principal, which Genie checks before answering
Grants on the agent's downstream dependencies, such as SELECT on its tables
questions.explanation: Granting access to a Genie Agent also requires granting its downstream dependencies (tables, warehouses, UC functions). Without SELECT, Genie returns empty results rather than errors.

questions.question: How should a client authenticate when it queries an agent hosted on Databricks Apps?
choices: With a SQL warehouse password
With an OAuth token; personal access tokens aren't supported for querying Apps
With a personal access token, which is the only method Databricks Apps accept for API calls
Anonymously, since Apps are public
questions.explanation: PATs are not supported for querying Databricks Apps; use an OAuth token. That nudges integrations toward short-lived, auditable credentials.

questions.question: What does Databricks recommend about service principals for apps?
choices: Share one service principal across every app in the workspace to simplify grants
Give each app's service principal workspace admin rights
Use one service principal per app and follow the principle of least privilege
Avoid service principals and use a developer's personal token instead
questions.explanation: Databricks recommends least privilege and one service principal per app. Shared service principals blur audit trails and widen blast radius.

questions.question: When agents.deploy() puts an agent on Model Serving, how does the agent authenticate to Databricks resources such as AI Search and UC functions?
choices: With the deploying user's personal access token, stored in the endpoint's environment variables in plain text for every request
It can't access them; agents on Model Serving can only call external APIs
With a workspace admin's credentials, refreshed every 90 days
Short-lived, minimum-permission credentials, after Databricks checks the endpoint owner's access
questions.explanation: deploy() provisions short-lived credentials for Databricks-managed resources declared by the agent, with minimum permissions, after verifying the endpoint owner has access. Non-Databricks secrets are passed as environment variables.

questions.question: What governance benefit do Databricks external model endpoints give for providers like OpenAI or Anthropic?
choices: API keys are stored centrally and encrypted, and calls go through one governed endpoint
Provider prices drop to the Databricks pay-per-token rate
They remove the need for a contract with the provider
Prompts never reach the provider, because Databricks answers from a local cache
questions.explanation: External model endpoints store keys centrally and encrypted (deleted with the endpoint) and can apply rate limits, usage tracking and guardrails. Providers include OpenAI and Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI and OpenAI-compatible custom endpoints.

questions.question: What does Azure Databricks say about data residency for Foundation Model APIs?
choices: Inputs and outputs are kept for seven years for model training
Data residency applies only to provisioned throughput, never to pay-per-token
A Designated Service using Azure Geographies; data may be kept up to 30 days for abuse detection
Data always leaves the customer's region for processing in the US, and Databricks makes no residency commitments for any model
questions.explanation: Foundation Model APIs are a Databricks Designated Service using Azure Geographies. The Model Serving page says pay-per-token inputs and outputs may be stored in the workspace region for up to 30 days for abuse detection. Partner providers may also retain data for safety.

questions.question: Which Model Serving endpoints support Private Link?
choices: Only external model endpoints
All endpoints, including pay-per-token and external models, as soon as the workspace itself is deployed with Private Link
None; Model Serving can't use Private Link
Provisioned throughput and custom model endpoints, but not external model endpoints by default
questions.explanation: The limits page says Private Link is supported only for provisioned throughput and custom endpoints. For strict network isolation, that steers production workloads toward provisioned throughput.

questions.question: Does Databricks AI Search enforce row-level or column-level security on index results?
choices: Only when the index is used through Copilot Studio
Yes. Unity Catalog row filters and column masks on the source table apply automatically to every index query result
Yes, but only for storage-optimized endpoints
No. Indexes are UC-governed, but row and column permissions aren't supported; filter in the app
questions.explanation: AI Search indexes appear in and are governed by Unity Catalog, but row- and column-level permissions aren't supported. The docs recommend application-level filters. For documents with mixed audiences, design separate indexes or filters.

questions.question: What permission does a Supervisor Agent's user need on a custom agent hosted on Databricks Apps?
choices: CAN USE on the app
EXECUTE on the app
None; Apps are open to all
SELECT on the app
questions.explanation: Supervisor permissions follow each subagent: access to a Genie Agent and its UC objects, CAN QUERY on serving endpoints, EXECUTE on UC functions, SELECT on tables and indexes, READ VOLUME on volumes, and CAN USE on custom MCP servers or agents on Apps.

questions.question: Which security and identity partners did Databricks name as upcoming Unity Gateway integrations?
choices: Security vendors such as CrowdStrike and Zscaler, and identity vendors such as Okta and SailPoint
Only Microsoft Purview and Microsoft Defender, through an exclusive partnership announced with Microsoft at the summit
Only Google Cloud Armor
None; Unity Gateway doesn't integrate with third-party security tools
questions.explanation: The June 2026 blog lists upcoming integrations with AI security vendors (including CrowdStrike, Cyera, Netskope, Palo Alto Networks and Zscaler) and identity vendors (Okta, Ping Identity, SailPoint, Saviynt). That helps customers keep their existing security stack.

questions.question: What does Unity Gateway's Smart Routing do?
choices: Routes requests to the most appropriate model based on task complexity, quality needs and cost
Routes Copilot requests to Genie
Routes failed requests to a human reviewer
Routes users to the nearest Azure region so that responses arrive faster, whichever model they choose
questions.explanation: The blog describes recommendations and routing to the most appropriate model by task complexity, quality requirements and cost. The overview mentions Smart Routing for coding tasks. It's a cost lever when teams default to the most expensive model.

questions.question: What are row filters and column masks in Unity Catalog?
choices: Dashboard filters that users pick to narrow what a chart shows during a session
Functions attached to tables that filter rows or mask column values depending on who is querying
Views that a data team copies for each department, with the rows that department may see
Settings in Genie that hide columns from answers but leave the underlying table unchanged for everyone
questions.explanation: Row filters and column masks are Unity Catalog functions attached to a table. Every Databricks query enforces them for the person querying, so Genie, dashboards, SQL and agents all respect them. Tables that use them aren't mirrored into Fabric.

questions.question: What is attribute-based access control (ABAC) in Unity Catalog?
choices: A list of approved attributes that agents may read from a user's Entra profile
Policies that apply row filters and column masks by governed tag, across many tables at once
A sign-in method that checks a user's device, network and location before opening the workspace
A Genie setting that answers differently depending on each user's job title
questions.explanation: ABAC lets you write a policy once, for example 'mask columns tagged PII for everyone outside HR', and apply it wherever the governed tag appears, instead of attaching filters and masks table by table. It scales governance as the number of tables grows.

questions.question: What is the Model Context Protocol (MCP)?
choices: An open protocol for connecting AI agents to tools and data
A security standard for encrypting prompts between agents
A Microsoft licensing model for agents that call other agents
A Databricks file format for packaging and deploying agents
questions.explanation: MCP is an open protocol that lets agents use tools and data sources. Databricks offers managed MCP servers for Genie and other services, and Unity Gateway can govern MCP services. It's how Genie plugs into Copilot Studio and Cowork.

questions.question: A team wants to call OpenAI and Anthropic models from Databricks with keys stored centrally, plus rate limits and logging. Which option fits?
choices: External model endpoints governed by Unity Gateway
Provisioned throughput for each vendor
API keys in each developer's notebook
A Genie Agent set to use those models
questions.explanation: External models route requests to third-party providers such as OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock and Google Vertex AI. Keys are stored centrally and encrypted, and Unity Gateway can add rate limits, logging to inference tables and guardrails. Keys in notebooks are hard to govern and rotate.

questions.question: What's the difference between Model Serving and Unity Gateway?
choices: Model Serving hosts models and agents as endpoints; Unity Gateway governs access to them
Model Serving is for batch jobs only; Unity Gateway is for real-time requests only
They're the same service: Unity Gateway is the new name for Model Serving in 2026
Model Serving governs external models; Unity Gateway hosts the Databricks-served models and agents
questions.explanation: Model Serving runs foundation models, custom models and agents as REST endpoints. Unity Gateway sits in front of models (Databricks-hosted and external), MCP services, UC functions and HTTP connections, adding usage tracking, inference tables, rate limits, fallbacks, budgets, guardrails and service policies.

questions.question: Row filters, ABAC policies and dynamic views can all limit what users see. How do they differ?
choices: Row filters work only in Genie; ABAC works only in dashboards; dynamic views work only when queried from notebooks
Row filters apply by tag across many tables; ABAC attaches to one table; dynamic views are the newest of the three patterns
Row filters attach to one table; ABAC applies them by tag across tables; dynamic views are the older pattern
They're three names for the same feature, and Unity Catalog converts each one into the others automatically
